name: Sheetali Breathing
intro:
Sheetali Breathing (Sheetali Pranayama) is a cooling breathing technique in yoga that helps calm the body and mind. It is especially useful for reducing body heat, stress, and mental agitation. In this practice, the breath is drawn in through a rolled tongue or pursed lips, creating a cooling sensation that helps lower internal temperature.

This pranayama is highly beneficial during hot weather or when the body feels overheated due to stress, anger, or physical exertion. It soothes the nervous system, slows down the heart rate, and promotes a sense of relaxation and balance.

Regular practice of Sheetali Breathing can help improve focus, reduce anxiety, and support overall emotional well-being. It is simple, effective, and suitable for beginners as well as experienced practitioners when done correctly.

steps.text: Sit comfortably in a cross-legged position with your spine straight.
Place your hands on your knees and relax your shoulders.
Roll your tongue into a tube shape (or purse your lips if unable to roll).
Inhale slowly through the rolled tongue or lips, feeling the cool air.
Close your mouth and hold the breath for a few seconds.
Repeat this cycle for 5-10 rounds, maintaining a calm rhythm.

benefits: Calms the mind and reduces stress
May help reduce high blood pressure
Promotes a feeling of freshness and calmness
Useful during hot weather or after physical exertion
avoid: You have respiratory issues like asthma (consult a doctor before practice)
You are suffering from low blood pressure
You have a cold, cough, or throat infection
You are in a very cold environment
You experience discomfort while inhaling through the mouth
